questions.q: What do all three staging models in this lesson have in common structurally?
options: Each joins two raw tables together
Each uses one source CTE followed by a flat select that only renames and casts columns, with no joins or aggregation
Each contains a GROUP BY to produce a summary
Each references another staging model with ref()
questions.explain: Every staging model follows the same narrow shape planned in Lesson 7: a source CTE, then a flat rename-only select.

questions.q: Why are all three staging models grouped under models/staging/jaffle_shop/ rather than a flat models/ folder?
options: dbt requires every model to be in its own uniquely named folder
Grouping models by source keeps the project navigable, and gives a future second source (added in Chapter 5) its own sibling folder instead of mixing in
Folder structure affects query performance in Snowflake
It is required for dbt build --select staging to work at all
questions.explain: Folder-per-source is a real, scalable convention — not a dbt requirement, but a maintainability choice that pays off as more sources are added.

questions.q: What does dbt build --select staging do?
options: Builds every model in the entire project regardless of folder
Builds (and tests, once added) only the models under the staging folder/selector, without touching marts
Deletes all staging models and rebuilds them from scratch
Only validates YAML syntax without running any SQL
questions.explain: The --select staging flag scopes the build to just the staging models, letting them be verified independently of the marts layer.

questions.q: In stg_jaffle_shop__payments.sql, what does the raw id column become?
options: order_id
customer_id
payment_id
amount
questions.explain: raw_payments.id is renamed to payment_id in the staged model, matching the planned convention for readable, consistent naming.

questions.q: What is the correct way to confirm all three staging models succeeded after running dbt build --select staging?
options: Trust the green terminal output alone with no further check
Run a plain SELECT ... LIMIT 10 against each resulting table in Snowflake and match column names against the Lesson 7 plan
Delete the raw tables to force a fresh rebuild
Check only that the dbt build command exited without printing anything
questions.explain: Confirming in Snowflake directly — checking real rows and real column names — is the real verification, not just trusting the build log.
